subTasks.name: General Chat & Writing
subTasks.description: Open-ended conversation and original prose production from a text prompt: answering, drafting, rewriting for tone, creative and persuasive writing, multilingual composition.

subTasks.name: Reasoning & Analysis
subTasks.description: Deriving a non-retrievable answer from a text prompt through multi-step inference: deduction, quantitative and symbolic reasoning, causal analysis, planning under constraints, argument evaluation.

subTasks.name: Coding
subTasks.description: Producing, reading, repairing or transforming source code and code-adjacent artefacts (SQL, regex, tests) from a natural-language or code text prompt.

subTasks.name: Text Processing
subTasks.description: Deterministic transformation of supplied text into a shorter, cleaner, translated, labelled or machine-readable form; the answer is contained in the input rather than generated from world knowledge.

subTasks.name: Image Generation & Editing
subTasks.description: Synthesising a new raster image from a text-only description, including in-image typography and explanatory illustration.

subTasks.name: Image Understanding
subTasks.description: Reading a supplied image and returning text: description, transcription, chart reading, detection and counting, visual question answering, interface and handwriting interpretation.

subTasks.name: Image Generation & Editing
subTasks.description: Transforming a supplied image into a new image under instruction: localised edits, restyling, and subject-consistent variation.

subTasks.name: Document Intelligence
subTasks.description: Reading a supplied document file (PDF or equivalent) with its layout intact and returning grounded text: structure, fields, tables, cross-page reasoning, answers with citations.

subTasks.name: Text Processing
subTasks.description: Applying text-processing operations - summarisation, translation, classification - to the full text of a supplied document file rather than to pasted text.

subTasks.name: Document Creation & Transformation
subTasks.description: Producing a new document artefact from a supplied document: format conversion with structure preserved, tracked rewriting, and template population.

subTasks.name: Data Intelligence
subTasks.description: Reading supplied structured data (CSV, JSON, table) and returning a natural-language reading of it: interpretation, statistical narration, anomaly explanation, insight.

subTasks.name: Data Intelligence
subTasks.description: Transforming supplied structured data into structured data: schema mapping, cleaning, deduplication and computed aggregation, emitted as valid machine-readable output.

subTasks.name: Data Intelligence
subTasks.description: Rendering supplied structured data as a visual artefact: charts and data-driven infographics.

subTasks.name: Embeddings & Retrieval
subTasks.description: Encoding text into a dense vector for semantic search, clustering and retrieval.

subTasks.name: Embeddings & Retrieval
subTasks.description: Encoding an image into a dense vector in a space shared with text, for cross-modal retrieval.

subTasks.name: Embeddings & Retrieval
subTasks.description: Encoding document passages or chunks into dense vectors for retrieval-augmented generation over document corpora.

miniTasks.name: Conversational Response
miniTasks.definition: Producing a direct, relevant, correctly scoped reply to a conversational turn, without adding unrequested content.
examples: What is the difference between a virus and a bacterium? Answer in two sentences.
I have thirty minutes before a meeting and I am nervous about it. What should I do?
Explain why the sky is blue to someone with no science background.
miniTasks.criteria: All three replies must be on-topic, factually correct, respect the stated length or audience constraint, and contain no refusal, no preamble padding and no invented follow-up questions.

miniTasks.name: Long-Form Content Drafting
miniTasks.definition: Generating an extended, internally coherent piece of original prose with a stated structure and length.
examples: Write a 600-word blog post on why small teams should document decisions, with an intro, three sections and a conclusion.
Draft a 500-word onboarding email sequence outline for a language-learning app, three emails, each with a subject line.
Write a 700-word explainer on how public transport fares are set, with subheadings.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must hit the requested length within +/-20%, contain every requested structural element, maintain one consistent thesis, and avoid repeated paragraphs or filler restatement.

miniTasks.name: Style & Tone Transformation
miniTasks.definition: Rewriting supplied text into a specified register, voice or reading level while preserving its propositional content exactly.
examples: Rewrite this in formal business English, changing no facts: 'hey we cant ship friday, the api broke, need till weds'.
Rewrite this sentence for an eight-year-old reader: 'Photosynthesis converts radiant energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.'
Rewrite this rejection note to be warmer without promising anything: 'Your application was unsuccessful. We will not be proceeding.'
miniTasks.criteria: All three rewrites must preserve every fact and commitment in the source, adopt the named register, add no new claims, and drop no stated condition.

miniTasks.name: Creative Narrative Generation
miniTasks.definition: Producing original fiction or narrative writing that satisfies stated creative constraints.
examples: Write a 150-word short story that begins and ends with the same sentence.
Write a six-line poem about a monsoon commute that does not use the words rain, wet or water.
Write a 200-word scene between two characters where the conflict is never stated out loud.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must obey the stated formal constraint exactly, be original rather than a retold known work, and remain coherent as a narrative.

miniTasks.name: Persuasive & Marketing Copywriting
miniTasks.definition: Writing short-form persuasive copy to a brief, with an explicit audience, benefit and call to action.
examples: Write three Google Search ad headlines under 30 characters each for a spoken-English app aimed at first-time smartphone users.
Write a 40-word app-store short description for a voice-to-text keyboard, leading with the main benefit.
Write two variants of a push notification (under 90 characters) that brings a lapsed learner back for a five-minute lesson.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must respect every stated character or word limit, name a concrete benefit, include the requested number of variants, and avoid unverifiable superlatives.

miniTasks.name: Multilingual Text Generation
miniTasks.definition: Composing original, idiomatic text directly in a specified non-English language, not translating from English.
examples: Write a 60-word product announcement in Hindi (Devanagari script) for a free daily speaking practice feature.
Write a polite three-sentence customer apology in Spanish for a delayed delivery.
Write a four-line congratulatory message in Tamil for a student who passed an exam.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must be written in the requested language and script, be grammatical and idiomatic for a native reader, respect the length limit, and contain no English fallback or transliteration.

miniTasks.name: Multi-Step Logical Deduction
miniTasks.definition: Reaching a conclusion that requires chaining two or more stated premises, where no single premise gives the answer.
examples: Five houses in a row. The red house is immediately left of the blue one. The green house is at one end. Blue is not at either end. Where can green be?
All auditors are accountants. Some accountants are not certified. Priya is an auditor. What can and cannot be concluded about Priya's certification?
A is heavier than B. C is lighter than B but heavier than D. Order all four from heaviest to lightest, or say if it is impossible.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must be logically correct, state the conclusion explicitly, and correctly flag any case that is underdetermined instead of guessing.

miniTasks.name: Arithmetic & Quantitative Reasoning
miniTasks.definition: Performing multi-step numerical computation from a word problem and reporting a correct final number with units.
examples: A subscription is 399 rupees a month or 3,588 a year. What is the percentage saving on the annual plan, to one decimal place?
A tank fills in 6 hours through pipe A and 9 hours through pipe B. Both open, how long to fill it? Give the answer in hours and minutes.
Cost per install is 18 rupees, install-to-trial is 22%, trial-to-paid is 14%. What is the cost per paid user?
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must be arithmetically exact, carry the correct units, respect the requested rounding, and show a computation path that actually produces the stated number.

miniTasks.name: Symbolic & Algebraic Problem Solving
miniTasks.definition: Manipulating symbolic expressions or equations to produce a correct closed form or solution set.
examples: Solve for x: (2x - 3)/(x + 4) = 5. State any excluded value.
Factor completely: 6x^3 - 9x^2 - 6x.
Given f(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 7, find the vertex and state whether it is a minimum or a maximum.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must be algebraically correct, include the full solution set, note domain exclusions where they exist, and not substitute numeric approximation for the requested symbolic form.

miniTasks.name: Causal & Counterfactual Analysis
miniTasks.definition: Distinguishing causal from correlational claims and reasoning about what would follow under a changed condition.
examples: Ice-cream sales and drowning deaths rise together each summer. Explain what this does and does not show, and name the likely confounder.
Trial conversion rose 8% the same week we cut price and changed the onboarding video. What would you need in order to attribute the lift to either change?
If a company had not raised prices last year but everything else held, what would you expect to happen to revenue, and what makes that prediction uncertain?
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must separate correlation from causation explicitly, name a concrete confounder or identification requirement, and avoid asserting a causal conclusion the evidence does not support.

miniTasks.name: Constraint Satisfaction & Planning
miniTasks.definition: Producing a plan or assignment that simultaneously satisfies every stated hard constraint, or proving none exists.
examples: Schedule four 1-hour interviews between 10:00 and 15:00 with a 1-hour lunch at 12:00, no two back-to-back. Give the timetable or say it is impossible.
Seat six people at a round table where A must sit next to B, C must not sit next to B, and D must sit opposite A. Give one valid seating.
Pack a 20 kg allowance from items weighing 9, 8, 6, 5 and 3 kg, maximising weight without exceeding it. List the items and the total.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must satisfy every hard constraint with no violation, state the solution concretely, and correctly declare infeasibility rather than relaxing a constraint silently.

miniTasks.name: Argument Evaluation & Fallacy Detection
miniTasks.definition: Assessing the validity of a supplied argument and naming the specific reasoning defect where one exists.
examples: 'Every successful founder I know dropped out, so dropping out causes success.' Name the flaw and explain it in two sentences.
'The policy must be wrong because it was proposed by someone with no economics degree.' Is this a good argument? Name the fallacy if there is one.
'If we allow remote work on Fridays, soon nobody will come in at all.' Evaluate this argument's structure.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must name the specific defect correctly, explain why it undermines the inference, and not simply agree or disagree with the conclusion.

miniTasks.name: Closed-Book Factual Recall
miniTasks.definition: Retrieving stable, verifiable world knowledge from parameters without tools, including correctly declining when uncertain.
examples: Name the three branches of the United States federal government and the primary function of each.
In which year was the Indian Constitution adopted, and in which year did it come into effect?
What are the four chambers of the human heart, and which one pumps blood into the aorta?
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must be factually correct on stable, non-time-sensitive knowledge, complete on every part asked, and contain no fabricated specifics.

miniTasks.name: Ambiguity Detection & Clarification
miniTasks.definition: Identifying that a request is underspecified and naming the specific missing information rather than guessing.
examples: 'Make the report shorter.' What do you need to know before doing this? List the missing information.
'Book it for next Friday.' Identify every ambiguity in this instruction.
'Compare the two plans and pick the better one.' What is undefined here, and what would you need to decide?
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must identify the genuine ambiguity, name the specific missing parameters, and not fabricate an answer as though the request were fully specified.

miniTasks.name: Code Generation from Specification
miniTasks.definition: Writing new, runnable source code that implements a stated behavioural specification.
examples: Write a Python function that takes a list of dicts with 'name' and 'score' and returns the top 3 names by score, ties broken alphabetically.
Write a JavaScript function that debounces a callback with a configurable delay and returns a cancel handle.
Write a Python function that validates an Indian mobile number (10 digits, starting 6-9) and returns True or False.
miniTasks.criteria: All three programs must run without syntax errors, implement the stated behaviour including the stated edge case, and handle empty or malformed input without raising an unhandled exception.

miniTasks.name: Code Debugging & Error Diagnosis
miniTasks.definition: Locating the defect in supplied code or a stack trace and stating the specific fix.
examples: This returns 0 for every input: `def avg(xs): total = 0; for x in xs: total += x; return total // len(xs) * 1.0`. Find and fix the bug.
A Python loop raises 'RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration'. Explain the cause and give the corrected pattern.
This SQL returns duplicate rows after adding a join to order_items. Explain why and give the corrected query shape.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must identify the actual root cause (not a symptom), give a corrected version that resolves it, and not introduce a new defect.

miniTasks.name: Code Explanation
miniTasks.definition: Explaining what supplied code does, in prose, without changing it.
examples: Explain what this does line by line: `result = [x**2 for x in range(10) if x % 3 == 0]`.
Explain what this regex matches and give one string it accepts and one it rejects: `^[A-Z]{2}\d{4}[A-Z]?$`.
Explain the difference in behaviour between `a = b` and `a = b[:]` for a Python list.
miniTasks.criteria: All three explanations must be accurate to the actual semantics, cover the specific construct asked about, and include the requested examples where asked.

miniTasks.name: Code Translation Across Languages
miniTasks.definition: Rewriting working code from one programming language into another with equivalent behaviour and idioms.
examples: Translate this Python to JavaScript: `def slugify(s): return '-'.join(s.lower().split())`.
Translate this JavaScript to Python: `const sum = arr.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);`.
Translate this SQL window function into equivalent Python pandas code: `SELECT id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY score DESC) FROM users`.
miniTasks.criteria: All three translations must be behaviourally equivalent on normal input, use idiomatic constructs of the target language, and preserve edge-case semantics such as empty-input handling.

miniTasks.name: Code Refactoring & Optimisation
miniTasks.definition: Restructuring working code to improve complexity, readability or resource use while preserving behaviour exactly.
examples: Refactor this O(n^2) duplicate finder into O(n): `dupes = [x for i,x in enumerate(xs) if x in xs[:i]]`.
Refactor this nested if-else chain of four levels into a flat guard-clause structure, keeping the same outcomes.
Reduce the memory footprint of a function that loads a 2 GB CSV fully into a list before summing one column.
miniTasks.criteria: All three refactors must preserve the original output for all valid inputs, deliver the stated improvement, and remain runnable.

miniTasks.name: Unit Test Generation
miniTasks.definition: Producing executable tests that cover the normal path plus meaningful edge and failure cases for supplied code.
examples: Write pytest tests for a function `discount(price, pct)` that raises ValueError if pct is outside 0-100.
Write Jest tests for a `formatCurrency(amount, currency)` function including zero, negative and very large values.
Write pytest tests for a function that parses 'DD/MM/YYYY' strings, including an invalid date such as 31/02/2025.
miniTasks.criteria: All three test suites must be syntactically valid in the named framework, include at least one boundary and one failure case, and assert on specific expected values rather than only on non-nullness.

miniTasks.name: SQL Query Authoring
miniTasks.definition: Writing a correct SQL query against a described schema, including joins, grouping and window logic.
examples: Given users(id, city, created_at) and payments(user_id, amount, paid_at), write SQL for revenue per city for the last 30 days.
Write SQL returning each user's first payment date and the number of days to their second payment, excluding users with one payment.
Write SQL that finds the top 3 products by units sold per category, using a window function.
miniTasks.criteria: All three queries must be valid SQL, join on the correct keys, group and filter as asked, and avoid returning duplicated rows from fan-out joins.

miniTasks.name: Regular Expression Construction
miniTasks.definition: Producing a regular expression that matches exactly the described set of strings and no more.
examples: Write a regex matching an Indian PAN number: five letters, four digits, one letter, all uppercase.
Write a regex that extracts the domain from an email address, capturing it in a group.
Write a regex matching a 24-hour time from 00:00 to 23:59 and rejecting 24:00 and 12:60.
miniTasks.criteria: All three expressions must match every positive case, reject every stated negative case, anchor correctly where required, and be syntactically valid in a standard regex engine.

miniTasks.name: Abstractive Text Summarisation
miniTasks.definition: Condensing supplied text into a shorter form in new wording, preserving the source's claims and adding none.
examples: Summarise this 600-word meeting transcript in exactly five bullet points, one per decision taken. [transcript supplied]
Summarise the following support ticket thread in two sentences for a manager. [thread supplied]
Reduce this 300-word product description to a 40-word summary keeping all three differentiators. [description supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three summaries must respect the stated length or count, cover every element the prompt required, introduce no fact absent from the source, and avoid copying long verbatim spans.

miniTasks.name: Language Translation
miniTasks.definition: Rendering supplied text into a target language with meaning, register and named entities preserved.
examples: Translate into Hindi, keeping product names in English: 'Your free trial ends tomorrow. Upgrade to keep your daily speaking streak.'
Translate this Spanish support message into English: 'No puedo iniciar sesion desde ayer; me dice que la contrasena es incorrecta.'
Translate into Telugu, keeping the polite register: 'Thank you for your patience. Our team will call you within 24 hours.'
miniTasks.criteria: All three translations must be accurate and idiomatic in the target language and script, preserve register and named entities as instructed, and omit or add no content.

miniTasks.name: Named Entity Extraction
miniTasks.definition: Identifying and returning the specific entity spans of requested types from supplied text.
examples: Extract every person name, organisation and date from: 'Ravi Menon joined Acme Labs on 3 March 2024 after four years at Northwind.'
List all monetary amounts and currencies in: 'The invoice totalled $4,200 plus GST of Rs 18,900, with a $150 credit applied.'
Extract all locations and phone numbers from: 'Call our Chennai desk on 044-2233-4455 or the Pune office on +91 20 4455 6677.'
miniTasks.criteria: All three extractions must return every instance of the requested types, return no entity of an unrequested type, and reproduce the spans exactly as they appear.

miniTasks.name: Text Classification & Labelling
miniTasks.definition: Assigning supplied text to a label from a closed, prompt-supplied label set.
examples: Classify as Billing, Technical or Account: 'The app crashes every time I open the lesson screen.' Return only the label.
Label this review as Spam or Not Spam: 'BUY CHEAP FOLLOWERS NOW visit my page link in bio!!!' Return only the label.
Classify the intent as Cancel, Upgrade or Query: 'How much extra is the yearly plan compared to monthly?' Return only the label.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must return exactly one label from the supplied set, choose the correct label, and include no explanation when the prompt asks for the label only.

miniTasks.name: Sentiment & Emotion Detection
miniTasks.definition: Determining the affective polarity or emotional state expressed in supplied text, including mixed and ironic cases.
examples: Give the sentiment as Positive, Negative or Mixed: 'Great teachers, but the app logs me out constantly.'
Identify the dominant emotion in: 'I've been waiting eleven days and nobody has replied. Unbelievable.'
Give the sentiment of: 'Oh brilliant, another update that removed the feature I actually used.'
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must select the correct polarity or emotion, correctly identify mixed sentiment where both valences are present, and not read irony as literal praise.

miniTasks.name: Keyword & Topic Extraction
miniTasks.definition: Identifying the salient terms or themes in supplied text without inventing terms absent from it.
examples: Extract the five most important keywords from this 400-word article. [article supplied]
List the three topics discussed in this customer call transcript, one short phrase each. [transcript supplied]
Give the six terms that best describe this product page for search indexing. [page supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must return exactly the requested count, use terms present in or directly supported by the source, and avoid generic filler terms that describe any document.

miniTasks.name: Grammar & Mechanics Correction
miniTasks.definition: Correcting grammatical, spelling and punctuation errors in supplied text while preserving the author's meaning and voice.
examples: Correct this without changing meaning: 'Their going to send the invoice's tomorrow, if thats ok with you.'
Fix the grammar and punctuation: 'we has recieved you're application and will responded shortly'.
Correct this sentence and say what was wrong: 'Neither the manager nor the engineers was aware of the outage.'
miniTasks.criteria: All three corrections must fix every actual error, introduce no new error, preserve the original meaning and register, and correctly identify the rule when asked.

miniTasks.name: Text-to-Schema JSON Generation
miniTasks.definition: Emitting syntactically valid JSON that conforms exactly to a schema stated in the prompt, from unstructured text.
examples: Return JSON with keys name, email, company from: 'Hi, I'm Anita Rao from Bluewave, reach me at anita@bluewave.io'. No other keys.
Return a JSON array of objects with keys item and qty from: 'two laptops, one docking station and four cables'.
Return JSON with keys date (ISO 8601), amount (number) and currency from: 'Paid Rs 12,500 on 14 August 2025'.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must parse as valid JSON, contain exactly the specified keys with no extras, use the specified value types and formats, and include no prose or code fence around the object.

miniTasks.name: Text Redaction & PII Masking
miniTasks.definition: Removing or masking specified sensitive spans in supplied text while leaving all other content intact.
examples: Redact all email addresses and phone numbers, replacing each with [REDACTED]: 'Reach Sunil at sunil.k@corp.in or 98765 43210 after 6pm.'
Mask all but the last four digits of any card or account number in: 'Charged to card 4111 1111 1111 1234 and account 000123456789.'
Remove every person name but keep job titles: 'Meera Iyer, Head of Design, briefed Arjun Rao, the new PM, on Tuesday.'
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must redact every instance of the targeted category, leave all non-targeted text byte-identical, apply the exact masking format requested, and over-redact nothing.

miniTasks.name: Text-to-Image Synthesis
miniTasks.definition: Generating a raster image that depicts the subject, composition and style described in a text-only prompt.
examples: Generate a photorealistic image of a woman in her thirties studying on a train at dusk, warm window light, shot on 50mm.
Generate a flat vector-style illustration of a mobile phone with a speech bubble, teal and cream palette, white background.
Generate a top-down photograph of a wooden desk with a notebook, a cup of chai and headphones, soft daylight.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must be returned as actual image data, contain every named subject element, follow the stated style and lighting direction, and be free of gross anatomical or structural artefacts.

miniTasks.name: In-Image Text Rendering
miniTasks.definition: Generating an image containing specified words rendered legibly and spelled correctly.
examples: Generate a square poster with the headline 'SPEAK ENGLISH DAILY' in bold sans-serif on a dark blue background, spelled exactly.
Generate a shop signboard image reading 'Sharma Electronics - Since 1994', text sharp and correctly spelled.
Generate an app-store screenshot mock with the caption '5 minutes a day' at the top, clean sans-serif type.
miniTasks.criteria: All three images must render the requested words with correct spelling and no dropped or duplicated characters, keep the text legible at full size, and place it as directed.

miniTasks.name: Explanatory Illustration Generation
miniTasks.definition: Generating a diagrammatic or instructional image whose spatial arrangement carries the intended meaning.
examples: Generate a simple labelled diagram of the water cycle with arrows for evaporation, condensation and precipitation.
Generate a three-step illustrated sequence showing a user installing an app: tap, download, open.
Generate a clean diagram of a funnel with four narrowing stages, top widest, labelled 1 to 4.
miniTasks.criteria: All three images must be structurally correct for the concept, order and connect the elements as described, keep any labels legible, and avoid decorative elements that contradict the diagram's logic.

miniTasks.name: Image Captioning & Description
miniTasks.definition: Producing an accurate natural-language description of a supplied image's content at the requested level of detail.
examples: Describe this photograph in two sentences, covering the setting and the main subject. [image supplied]
Write alt text under 125 characters for this image for a screen reader. [image supplied]
List the five most prominent objects in this image in order of visual prominence. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must describe only what is actually present in the image, respect the stated length or count, and contain no hallucinated object, text or person.

miniTasks.name: Optical Character Recognition
miniTasks.definition: Transcribing printed text visible in a supplied image, preserving reading order and characters exactly.
examples: Transcribe all text in this photographed receipt exactly as printed, preserving line order. [image supplied]
Read the text on this product label and return it verbatim, including the units. [image supplied]
Transcribe the text in this screenshot, keeping the original line breaks. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three transcriptions must reproduce the visible characters accurately including digits and punctuation, preserve reading order, omit no visible line, and invent no text.

miniTasks.name: Chart & Graph Reading
miniTasks.definition: Extracting specific values, trends or comparisons from a chart image.
examples: From this bar chart, give the value for March and say which month is highest. [image supplied]
From this line chart, describe the trend between 2021 and 2024 and state the approximate peak value. [image supplied]
From this pie chart, list each segment with its percentage in descending order. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must read the axes and legend correctly, report values consistent with the plotted data, identify the correct extremum, and not infer data points that are not shown.

miniTasks.name: Object Detection & Counting
miniTasks.definition: Identifying the presence, count and relative position of specified objects in a supplied image.
examples: How many people are visible in this image, and how many are wearing helmets? [image supplied]
Is there a traffic sign in this image? If so, what type and where in the frame? [image supplied]
Count the number of chairs and state whether any are occupied. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must give a count that matches the image, correctly report presence or absence, describe position accurately, and state uncertainty rather than guessing when the image is ambiguous.

miniTasks.name: Visual Question Answering
miniTasks.definition: Answering a specific question that requires inspecting a supplied image rather than general knowledge.
examples: What time does the clock in this photograph show? [image supplied]
Based on this image, is this door push or pull, and how can you tell? [image supplied]
Which of the two boxes in this image is taller, and roughly by how much? [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must be grounded in visible evidence, cite the visual cue that supports the answer where asked, and decline to answer if the image does not contain the information.

miniTasks.name: Interface Screenshot Interpretation
miniTasks.definition: Reading a user-interface screenshot and describing its structure, controls and state.
examples: From this app screenshot, list every tappable control and what each appears to do. [image supplied]
In this settings screen, which toggles are on and which are off? [image supplied]
Describe the navigation hierarchy shown in this screenshot and name the currently active tab. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must correctly identify the visible controls and their states, distinguish active from inactive elements, and not invent controls that are absent.

miniTasks.name: Handwriting Recognition
miniTasks.definition: Transcribing handwritten text from a supplied image.
examples: Transcribe this handwritten note as accurately as possible, marking illegible words as [illegible]. [image supplied]
Read the handwritten figures on this form and return them as a list. [image supplied]
Transcribe the handwritten name and date at the bottom of this document. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three transcriptions must recover the legible content accurately, mark genuinely illegible spans rather than guessing, and preserve digits exactly.

miniTasks.name: Instruction-Guided Image Editing
miniTasks.definition: Applying a described localised modification to a supplied image while leaving the rest unchanged.
examples: In this photo, replace the background with a plain light-grey studio backdrop, keeping the subject unchanged. [image supplied]
Remove the parked car on the left from this street photo and fill the space plausibly. [image supplied]
Change the colour of the jacket in this image from red to navy, keeping texture and folds. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must be returned as images, apply the requested edit accurately, leave unmentioned regions visually unchanged, and show no obvious seam or smear at the edit boundary.

miniTasks.name: Image Style Transfer
miniTasks.definition: Re-rendering a supplied image in a specified visual style while preserving its composition and subject.
examples: Re-render this photograph as a flat vector illustration with three colours, keeping the composition. [image supplied]
Convert this colour photo to a high-contrast black-and-white film look, preserving all detail. [image supplied]
Redraw this product photo as a clean line-art sketch on white. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must preserve the original subject and layout, apply the named style consistently across the frame, and not add or remove subject elements.

miniTasks.name: Subject-Consistent Image Variation
miniTasks.definition: Generating a new image that keeps a supplied subject's identity while changing pose, setting or framing.
examples: Generate the same character from this image now seated at a desk, same face and clothing. [image supplied]
Produce a wide-shot version of this product on the same surface, same product, different angle. [image supplied]
Generate this same mascot waving, keeping proportions and colours identical. [image supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must preserve recognisable subject identity, colours and proportions, apply the requested change in pose or framing, and avoid drifting into a visibly different subject.

miniTasks.name: Document Layout Understanding
miniTasks.definition: Recognising a document's structural elements - headings, sections, columns, headers, footnotes - from the file itself.
examples: From this PDF, list every top-level section heading in document order. [PDF supplied]
Identify which parts of this PDF page are header, body, footnote and page number. [PDF supplied]
Does this PDF use a single or multi-column layout, and where does the reading order break across pages? [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must reflect the document's actual visual structure, preserve document order, distinguish body text from furniture such as headers and footers, and not conflate the two.

miniTasks.name: Document Field Extraction
miniTasks.definition: Pulling specific named field values out of a form-like document, correctly located and typed.
examples: From this invoice PDF, extract invoice number, invoice date, tax amount and grand total. [PDF supplied]
From this purchase order, extract vendor name, PO number, delivery date and payment terms. [PDF supplied]
From this ID form, extract full name, date of birth and issuing authority. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three extractions must return the correct value for every requested field, take values from the correct label rather than a visually adjacent one, preserve number and date formatting faithfully, and mark a field absent rather than inventing it.

miniTasks.name: Table Extraction from Documents
miniTasks.definition: Recovering tabular data from a document with row, column and header relationships intact.
examples: Extract the line-items table from this invoice PDF with all columns and rows, preserving header names. [PDF supplied]
From this report PDF, extract Table 2 including merged header cells and any footnote markers. [PDF supplied]
Extract the table that spans pages 4 and 5 of this PDF as a single table. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three extractions must preserve the correct row-column alignment, keep header names, handle merged cells and page-spanning tables without dropping rows, and not shift values between columns.

miniTasks.name: Multi-Page Cross-Reference Reasoning
miniTasks.definition: Answering a question that requires combining information located on different pages of one document.
examples: In this PDF, does the total on page 8 match the sum of the line items on pages 3 to 5? Show the comparison. [PDF supplied]
This contract defines 'Services' on page 2 and uses the term on page 11. Explain what the page 11 clause actually obliges. [PDF supplied]
Find the figure referenced as 'Table 3' in the text and state which page it appears on and what it shows. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must correctly locate information on multiple distinct pages, combine it accurately, cite the pages used, and not answer from a single page alone.

miniTasks.name: Grounded Document Question Answering
miniTasks.definition: Answering a question strictly from a supplied document, and saying so when the document does not contain the answer.
examples: According to this policy PDF, what is the notice period for termination? [PDF supplied]
Does this document state a governing jurisdiction? If yes, which; if no, say it is not stated. [PDF supplied]
What is the stated warranty duration in this manual? [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must be supported by text actually present in the document, must not import outside knowledge, and must state explicitly when the document is silent instead of guessing.

miniTasks.name: Citation & Span Attribution
miniTasks.definition: Returning the exact location - page, section or quoted span - that supports an answer drawn from a document.
examples: Answer what the late-payment penalty is and give the page and clause number where it appears. [PDF supplied]
Quote the exact sentence in this PDF that defines the deliverable, and give its page. [PDF supplied]
For each of the three obligations you list, give the section number it comes from. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must give locations that actually contain the cited content, quote spans verbatim where quoting is asked, and attach an attribution to every claim requested.

miniTasks.name: Document Summarisation
miniTasks.definition: Summarising the content of a supplied document file at a stated length, covering the whole document rather than its first pages.
examples: Summarise this 20-page PDF report in 200 words, covering every major section. [PDF supplied]
Give a one-paragraph executive summary of this contract PDF, naming the parties and the term. [PDF supplied]
Summarise this PDF in five bullets, one per chapter. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three summaries must draw on the full document rather than the opening pages, respect the requested length or structure, cover every section asked for, and add no claim not present in the file.

miniTasks.name: Document Translation
miniTasks.definition: Translating the text content of a supplied document into a target language while preserving its structure.
examples: Translate this two-page PDF into Hindi, keeping the heading structure and numbering. [PDF supplied]
Translate the body text of this PDF into English, leaving all proper nouns and figures unchanged. [PDF supplied]
Translate this PDF form's labels into Tamil, keeping field order. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three translations must cover the full document, preserve headings, numbering and field order, leave figures and named entities intact as instructed, and omit no section.

miniTasks.name: Document Clause & Section Classification
miniTasks.definition: Assigning sections or clauses of a supplied document to categories from a closed label set.
examples: Label every clause in this contract PDF as Payment, Liability, Termination or Other. [PDF supplied]
For this policy PDF, mark each section as Mandatory Requirement or Guidance. [PDF supplied]
Classify each paragraph in this PDF as Background, Method, Result or Discussion. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must label every section in the document, use only labels from the supplied set, apply them correctly, and skip no clause.

miniTasks.name: Document Format Conversion
miniTasks.definition: Converting a supplied document into another document format with heading hierarchy, lists and tables preserved.
examples: Convert this PDF into clean Markdown, preserving heading levels, lists and tables. [PDF supplied]
Convert this PDF into structured HTML with semantic heading tags and table markup. [PDF supplied]
Convert this PDF's tables into CSV blocks and its prose into Markdown, keeping document order. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three conversions must preserve heading hierarchy, list nesting and table structure, keep the original document order, and drop no content section.

miniTasks.name: Document Rewriting & Redlining
miniTasks.definition: Producing a revised version of a supplied document with changes made and identified.
examples: Rewrite this PDF policy at a plain-English reading level and list every change you made. [PDF supplied]
Produce a redlined version of this contract clause set, marking insertions and deletions. [PDF supplied]
Shorten this PDF proposal by 30% without removing any commitment, and note what was cut. [PDF supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must return a complete revised document, mark or list every change made, preserve all substantive commitments, and not silently drop clauses.

miniTasks.name: Document Template Population
miniTasks.definition: Filling a supplied document template with supplied values, leaving the template structure intact.
examples: Fill this offer-letter template PDF with the supplied candidate name, role, start date and salary band. [PDF and values supplied]
Populate this invoice template with the supplied line items and compute the total. [PDF and values supplied]
Complete this report template's summary section using the supplied metrics. [PDF and values supplied]
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must place every value in the correct field, leave the template's structure and unfilled boilerplate intact, compute any derived value correctly, and leave no placeholder token unresolved.

miniTasks.name: Tabular Data Interpretation
miniTasks.definition: Reading a supplied table or CSV and answering questions about its contents in natural language.
examples: From this CSV of 200 sales rows, which region had the highest total revenue and by how much over second place?
In this JSON array of users, how many have a null 'city' field and what fraction is that?
From this table, describe how the conversion rate differs between the two cohorts.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must be arithmetically consistent with the supplied data, reference the correct columns, handle nulls explicitly, and not report figures absent from the data.

miniTasks.name: Statistical Summary Narration
miniTasks.definition: Computing and explaining descriptive statistics for a supplied dataset in prose.
examples: Give the mean, median and standard deviation of the 'amount' column in this CSV and explain what the gap between mean and median indicates.
Summarise the distribution of session lengths in this JSON, including the interquartile range.
Report the correlation between 'lessons_completed' and 'days_active' in this CSV and state whether it is strong.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must compute the statistics correctly from the supplied values, interpret them accurately, and avoid asserting causation from a correlation.

miniTasks.name: Anomaly & Outlier Explanation
miniTasks.definition: Identifying data points that deviate from the pattern in a supplied dataset and offering candidate explanations.
examples: In this CSV of daily signups, identify any outlier days and give a plausible reason to check for each.
This JSON of API latencies has a spike. Identify which entries are anomalous and by what threshold you judged them.
Find any rows in this table whose values are internally inconsistent and explain the inconsistency.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must identify the actual outlying rows, state the criterion used to call them outliers, and separate observed anomalies from speculated causes.

miniTasks.name: Data-Grounded Insight Generation
miniTasks.definition: Deriving a non-obvious, decision-relevant conclusion supported by the supplied data.
examples: From this CSV of campaign spend and installs, what should we stop funding and why? Cite the numbers.
Given this cohort retention table, what is the single biggest drop-off point and what does it suggest?
Given this pricing experiment data, does the variant justify rollout? Support the answer with the figures.
miniTasks.criteria: All three answers must cite specific values from the data, draw a conclusion that follows from them, and state the limitation or confound rather than overclaiming.

miniTasks.name: Schema Mapping & Transformation
miniTasks.definition: Converting supplied structured data from one schema or shape into another, emitting valid structured output.
examples: Convert this array of flat records into nested JSON grouped by 'city', with a 'users' array under each. Return JSON only.
Map this CSV's columns (fname, lname, mail) to a JSON schema with keys first_name, last_name, email. Return JSON only.
Transform this JSON of key-value pairs into a two-column CSV with headers 'key' and 'value'. Return CSV only.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must parse as valid JSON or CSV, use exactly the target schema's keys and types, retain every input record, and include no prose or code fence.

miniTasks.name: Data Cleaning & Normalisation
miniTasks.definition: Standardising formats, types and missing values in supplied structured data, returning structured output.
examples: Normalise every date in this CSV's 'date' column to ISO 8601 and return the corrected CSV.
In this JSON, trim whitespace, lowercase all emails and replace empty strings with null. Return JSON only.
Standardise the phone numbers in this CSV to E.164 for India and flag any that cannot be parsed. Return CSV only.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must be valid structured data, apply the normalisation to every affected row, leave conforming values untouched, and flag rather than silently drop unparseable values.

miniTasks.name: Record Deduplication & Entity Resolution
miniTasks.definition: Identifying records in supplied data that refer to the same entity and merging them under a stated rule.
examples: Deduplicate this JSON of contacts, treating same email as same person, keeping the most complete record. Return JSON only.
In this CSV, merge company rows that differ only by suffix ('Ltd', 'Limited', 'Pvt Ltd') and return the merged CSV.
Find near-duplicate rows in this dataset by name and phone, and return a JSON list of duplicate groups.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must correctly group the true duplicates, merge according to the stated rule, keep genuinely distinct records separate, and emit valid structured output.

miniTasks.name: Structured Aggregation & Computation
miniTasks.definition: Computing grouped aggregates or derived fields over supplied structured data and returning structured output.
examples: From this CSV of orders, return JSON with total revenue and order count per customer, sorted by revenue descending.
Add a computed 'margin_pct' column to this CSV, rounded to one decimal, and return the CSV.
From this JSON of events, return a JSON object with counts per event type per day.
miniTasks.criteria: All three outputs must be valid structured data, compute every aggregate correctly from the supplied rows, apply the requested sort, rounding and grouping, and omit no group.

miniTasks.name: Chart Rendering from Data
miniTasks.definition: Producing a chart image that accurately plots supplied structured data with correct axes and labels.
examples: Render a bar chart image of these twelve monthly revenue values with labelled axes and a title.
Render a line chart image showing these two series over the same date range, with a legend.
Render a horizontal bar chart of these category counts, sorted descending, with value labels.
miniTasks.criteria: All three images must plot every supplied data point at the correct relative magnitude, label axes and series as asked, apply the requested sort or series split, and misstate no value.

miniTasks.name: Data-Driven Infographic Generation
miniTasks.definition: Producing a composed visual summary image that presents supplied figures with correct values and readable typography.
examples: Create a single-panel infographic image presenting these four KPIs with their values and short labels.
Create a visual summary image of this funnel's four stages with the supplied counts and drop-off percentages.
Create a comparison graphic image for these three plans with the supplied prices and two features each.
miniTasks.criteria: All three images must display every supplied figure with correct values and spelling, keep all text legible, and arrange elements so the intended comparison reads correctly.

miniTasks.name: Semantic Text Embedding
miniTasks.definition: Encoding a text passage into a fixed-length dense vector whose geometry reflects semantic similarity.
examples: Embed this sentence and return the vector: 'How do I cancel my subscription?'
Embed these three sentences and rank them by cosine similarity to the query 'refund policy'.
Embed this 300-word support article as a single vector for a retrieval index.
miniTasks.criteria: All three calls must return numeric vectors of the model's stated fixed dimensionality, be deterministic for identical input, and rank semantically related text above unrelated text on cosine similarity.

miniTasks.name: Multilingual Text Embedding
miniTasks.definition: Encoding text in multiple languages into one shared vector space so that translations land close together.
examples: Embed 'How do I reset my password?' and its Hindi translation and report their cosine similarity.
Embed these five sentences across English, Spanish and Tamil and cluster them by meaning, not by language.
Embed a Telugu query and rank a set of English documents by relevance to it.
miniTasks.criteria: All three calls must place cross-lingual paraphrases closer than unrelated same-language text, return vectors of consistent dimensionality across languages, and not cluster purely by script.

miniTasks.name: Code Embedding
miniTasks.definition: Encoding source code into vectors whose similarity reflects functional rather than lexical resemblance.
examples: Embed this Python function and retrieve the most similar of three candidate implementations.
Embed a natural-language query 'parse a CSV and skip the header' and rank five code snippets by relevance.
Embed two functions that do the same thing in different languages and report their similarity.
miniTasks.criteria: All three calls must return code-appropriate vectors, rank functionally equivalent code above lexically similar but functionally different code, and support cross-language or text-to-code retrieval where asked.

miniTasks.name: Image Embedding
miniTasks.definition: Encoding an image into a dense vector, ideally in a space shared with text for cross-modal retrieval.
examples: Embed this product photo and return the vector. [image supplied]
Embed these four images and group them by visual subject.
Embed this image and rank three text captions by relevance to it.
miniTasks.criteria: All three calls must accept image input and return numeric vectors of fixed dimensionality, group visually similar images together, and support image-to-text ranking where a shared space is claimed.

miniTasks.name: Document Chunk Embedding
miniTasks.definition: Encoding passage-level chunks of a document into vectors suitable for retrieval-augmented generation.
examples: Embed each of these ten 500-token chunks from a policy document and return one vector per chunk.
Embed this document's chunks and return the three most relevant to the query 'notice period'.
Embed a mixed set of chunks from two documents and return them grouped by source document.
miniTasks.criteria: All three calls must return one vector per chunk with consistent dimensionality, retrieve the chunk that actually contains the answer at rank one where asked, and handle batch input without truncating the set.

miniTasks.name: Long-Passage Embedding
miniTasks.definition: Encoding a long passage - beyond a short-sentence window - into a single vector without silent truncation.
examples: Embed this 4,000-token document section as a single vector and state the token count consumed.
Embed two long sections of the same report and report their similarity.
Embed a long passage and confirm whether any input was truncated to fit the context window.
miniTasks.criteria: All three calls must accept the full passage within the model's documented context, report or avoid truncation rather than silently discarding text, and produce vectors that remain discriminative at long input length.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.tradeoff: Highest-intelligence OpenAI general model in the set; reference point for BEST on reasoning and coding sub-tasks.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.tradeoff: Balanced OpenAI tier: near-flagship quality at roughly half the output price of Terra.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.tradeoff: Low-cost member of the current OpenAI family; strong cost/intelligence balance for document and text work.

models.name: GPT-5 Nano
models.tradeoff: Ultra-low-cost multimodal-input option; anchors the cheap end of the OpenAI ladder.

models.name: GPT-5.3 Codex
models.tradeoff: Coding specialist; highest code axis in the set. Included for specialist capability, not general breadth.

models.name: GPT-OSS 120B
models.tradeoff: Open-weight, text-only, one of the cheapest capable reasoning models available; key low-cost coverage.

models.name: GPT-5.4 Image 2
models.tradeoff: High-fidelity image generation and editing with strong in-image text rendering.

models.name: GPT-5 Image Mini
models.tradeoff: Cheapest OpenAI image-output model; low-cost coverage for Text/Image to Image.

models.name: Text Embedding 3 Small
models.tradeoff: Cheapest widely-integrated embedding model; the default low-cost retrieval option.

models.name: Text Embedding 3 Large
models.tradeoff: Higher-quality OpenAI retrieval tier where recall accuracy matters more than cost.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.tradeoff: Highest overall intelligence in the curated set; BEST candidate on the hardest reasoning, coding and document sub-tasks.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.tradeoff: Frontier intelligence at one-half the Fable price; strongest document intelligence per rupee at the top tier.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.tradeoff: Balanced tier: close to Opus on most sub-tasks at 40% of the price. Strong default ALTERNATIVE.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.tradeoff: Cheapest Anthropic model with native document (file) input; low-cost document intelligence coverage.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.tradeoff: Best-in-set document and image understanding; very large context for multi-page reasoning.

models.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
models.tradeoff: Strong multimodal quality at mid-tier price; best cost/intelligence balance for vision and document work.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite
models.tradeoff: Low-cost multimodal workhorse with native file input; key cheap option for document and image tasks.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite
models.tradeoff: Cheapest model in the set that accepts image and document input; anchors low-cost multimodal coverage.

models.name: Gemini 3 Pro Image
models.tradeoff: Highest-quality image generation and instruction-guided editing, including chart and infographic rendering.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash Image
models.tradeoff: Mid-cost image generation with reliable edit fidelity; strong balance for Image to Image.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image
models.tradeoff: Cheapest image-output model in the set; makes image generation viable at scale.

models.name: Gemma 4 31B IT
models.tradeoff: Open-weight, very low cost, image-input capable; low-cost alternative when no document input is needed.

models.name: Gemini Embedding 2
models.tradeoff: Multimodal embedding covering text and image in one shared space; enables cross-modal retrieval.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.2
models.tradeoff: Meta's current multimodal flagship with native file input; broad coverage at mid price.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
models.tradeoff: Open-weight multimodal at very low cost; strong cheap option for image understanding.

models.name: Llama 4 Scout
models.tradeoff: Cheaper Llama 4 tier; low-cost coverage for text and basic vision.

models.name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
models.tradeoff: Floor-price text model; included to give the router a genuine bottom-of-market option for trivial text tasks.

models.name: Llama Guard 4 12B
models.tradeoff: Safety-classification specialist; cheap, deterministic labelling for moderation routing only.

models.name: Mistral Large 2512
models.tradeoff: European-hosted flagship with document input at well below frontier pricing.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.1
models.tradeoff: Mid-tier balance with file input; cheaper document intelligence than any frontier model.

models.name: Mistral Small 2603
models.tradeoff: Low-cost vision-capable text model; strong text-processing value.

models.name: Ministral 3B 2512
models.tradeoff: Near-floor pricing with image input; cheapest route for high-volume simple classification.

models.name: Codestral 2508
models.tradeoff: Dedicated code model at a fraction of general-model cost; cheapest capable option for routine code generation.

models.name: Mistral Embed
models.tradeoff: Low-cost European embedding option for text retrieval.

models.name: Codestral Embed
models.tradeoff: Code-specialised embedding model; materially better code retrieval than general text embeddings.

models.name: Grok 4.6
models.tradeoff: Frontier-class reasoning with document input at roughly a third of top-tier output price.

models.name: Grok 4.3
models.tradeoff: Cheapest frontier-adjacent model with file input; unusually low output price for its tier.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.tradeoff: Near-frontier reasoning and coding at roughly one-tenth frontier pricing; the key cost/intelligence outlier.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.tradeoff: Among the cheapest capable text models in the set; core low-cost coverage for text processing.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision
models.tradeoff: Adds image understanding to the DeepSeek cheap tier at minimal price increase.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Max
models.tradeoff: Strongest non-US general model in the set; strong multilingual and vision coverage.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Flash
models.tradeoff: Cheap multimodal-input tier with solid multilingual text processing.

models.name: Qwen3.7 Flash
models.tradeoff: Cheapest image-input model in the whole set; critical for low-cost vision routing.

models.name: Qwen3 Coder Next
models.tradeoff: Very low-cost coding specialist; cheapest capable option for code generation and translation.

models.name: Qwen3 Embedding 8B
models.tradeoff: Strong multilingual embeddings at one of the lowest prices on the platform.

models.name: Qwen3 Embedding 4B
models.tradeoff: Smaller, faster multilingual embedding tier for very high-volume indexing.

models.name: Nova Pro
models.tradeoff: Enterprise-supported multimodal model with strong AWS-side governance; mid-cost alternative.

models.name: Nova Lite
models.tradeoff: Very cheap vision-capable model; useful floor option for simple captioning and classification.

models.name: Nova Micro
models.tradeoff: Lowest-priced Amazon tier; text-only bulk processing.

models.name: Phi-4
models.tradeoff: Small open-weight model with unusually strong reasoning per parameter; cheap deterministic text work.

models.name: Command A
models.tradeoff: Enterprise retrieval-and-grounding specialist; strong structured and citation-oriented text output.

models.name: Command R7B
models.tradeoff: Near-floor pricing from an enterprise vendor; cheap extraction and classification.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B
models.tradeoff: Open-weight near-frontier text reasoning; self-hostable alternative to closed frontier models.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Super 120B
models.tradeoff: Very strong reasoning per dollar; one of the cheapest models above the 75 intelligence line.

models.name: GLM-5.3
models.tradeoff: High coding and reasoning scores at mid-tier pricing; strong BEST alternative for code sub-tasks.

models.name: GLM-5.3 Flash
models.tradeoff: Multimodal input at near-floor pricing; strong cheap option for vision plus text processing.

models.name: GLM-4.6V
models.tradeoff: Vision-first specialist: image understanding well above its price tier.

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.tradeoff: Balanced multimodal-input model with long context at low cost.

models.name: Kimi K2.6
models.tradeoff: Strong agentic and coding performance at well under frontier pricing.

models.name: Seed 2.0 Mini
models.tradeoff: Cheap multimodal-input tier; adds vendor diversity at the low-cost end.

models.name: Granite 4.1 8B
models.tradeoff: Enterprise-governed small open model with permissive licensing; cheap compliant text processing.

models.name: Voyage 4 Large
models.tradeoff: Highest retrieval quality in the embedding set; BEST candidate for Embeddings and Retrieval.

models.name: Voyage 4 Lite
models.tradeoff: Strong retrieval quality at the same price as the cheapest OpenAI embedding tier.

models.name: Voyage Multimodal 3.5
models.tradeoff: Image and document-page embeddings in a shared text space; specialist multimodal retrieval.

models.name: Voyage Code 4
models.tradeoff: Best code-retrieval embedding in the set; specialist for code search over general embeddings.
